title: Agent Reporting (v2)
description:
## What to build

Report pi agent status back to herdr via pane.report_agent, so herdr knows when pi is actively working in a pane. This is a v2 enhancement.

### API:
- `pane.report_agent` — report agent status (working, idle, error)
- `pane.report_agent_session` — report session metadata
- `pane.clear_agent_authority` — clear agent claim on pane
- `pane.release_agent` — release agent from pane

### Design decisions needed:
- When to report? (on tool call? on session start?)
- What status to report?
- Agent identity? (agent name, model, task description)

### Files:
- Extends `slices/pane/pane.tool.ts` or new `slices/agent/`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Agent reports status to herdr on session_start
- [ ] Agent clears authority on session_shutdown

## Blocked by
None - can start immediately

title: Event Subscriptions
description:
## What to build

Subscribe to herdr events and forward them to the pi agent via steering messages. Allows agent to react to pane changes, workspace switches, etc.

### Design decisions needed:
- Polling vs persistent connection pattern?
- Which events to subscribe to? (pane.focused, workspace.focused, pane.exited, etc.)
- How to throttle/rate-limit events?
- When to unsubscribe?

### Suggested events:
- pane.focused — notify agent when focus changes
- workspace.focused — notify agent when workspace changes
- pane.exited — notify agent when a process exits

### Files:
- `slices/events/events.types.ts` — EventName, EventSubscription
- `slices/events/events.ts` — event subscription logic

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Agent receives steering message on pane.focused
- [ ] Agent receives steering message on workspace.focused
- [ ] Clean subscription on session_shutdown
- [ ] Rate limiting to avoid spam

## Blocked by
- #1

title: Key Combos (send_keys)
description:
## What to build

Expose tool to send key combinations to a pane. Used for interrupting processes (ctrl+c), navigation, etc.

### Tool:
- `herdr_send_keys` — calls `pane.send_keys` with params { pane_id, keys: string[] }. Supports key combos like ["ctrl+c"], ["ctrl+d"], ["alt+x"], etc.

### Types:
- KeyCombo: string[] (list of key names to send)
- Supported keys: printable chars, enter, esc, tab, backspace, delete, ctrl+<key>, alt+<key>, f1-f12

### Files:
- `slices/keys/keys.types.ts` — KeyCombo, supported keys list
- `slices/keys/keys.tool.ts` — registerKeysTools

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `herdr_send_keys` sends key combos to pane
- [ ] ctrl+c works (interrupt process)
- [ ] ctrl+d works
- [ ] Error when pane_id invalid
- [ ] Supports multiple keys in sequence

## Blocked by
- #1

title: Pane Wait for Output
description:
## What to build

Expose tool to wait for a specific pattern in pane output. Essential for monitoring long-running commands.

### Tool:

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `herdr_pane_wait` waits for pattern in pane output
- [ ] Returns success when pattern found
- [ ] Timeout handling returns clear error
- [ ] Works with regex patterns
- [ ] Works with plain text patterns

title: Pane Send & Read
description:
## What to build

Expose pane interaction tools: send text/commands to a pane and read output from a pane.

### Tools:
- `herdr_pane_send_text` — calls `pane.send_text` with params { pane_id, text, execute?: boolean }. Sends command to pane.
- `herdr_pane_read` — calls `pane.read` with params { pane_id, lines?: number, timeout?: number }. Returns pane output text.

### Types:
- PaneSendOptions: { pane_id, text, execute? }
- PaneReadOptions: { pane_id, lines?, timeout? }

### Files:
- Extends `slices/pane/pane.types.ts`
- `slices/pane/pane.tool.ts` — registers herdr_pane_send_text, herdr_pane_read

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `herdr_pane_send_text` sends command to specified pane
- [ ] `herdr_pane_read` returns output from specified pane
- [ ] execute flag works (send + enter vs just type text)
- [ ] lines parameter limits output
- [ ] timeout parameter works
- [ ] Error when pane_id invalid

title: SKILL.md + Prompt Templates
description:
## What to build

Create SKILL.md that teaches the pi agent how to use herdr tools effectively, and prompt templates for common workflows.

### Skill:
- `skill/SKILL.md` with frontmatter (name: pi-herdr, description)
- Instructions: always connect first, use 3-step pattern (send → wait → read), use wait for long commands, use key combos for interrupts, export layout before experiments

### Prompt Templates:
- `prompts/run-and-observe.md` — chain: herdr_pane_send_text → herdr_pane_wait → herdr_pane_read
- `prompts/debug-terminal.md` — chain: herdr_pane_split → send debug command → read output
- `prompts/setup-workspace.md` — chain: focus workspace → split panes → send setup commands
- `prompts/export-layout.md` — chain: herdr_layout_export → save layout

### Files:
- `skill/SKILL.md`
- `prompts/run-and-observe.md`
- `prompts/debug-terminal.md`
- `prompts/setup-workspace.md`
- `prompts/export-layout.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SKILL.md has correct frontmatter (name, description)
- [ ] SKILL.md explains 3-step pattern (send → wait → read)
- [ ] Prompt templates follow crew-of-pi chain format
- [ ] Templates reference correct tool names

## Blocked by
None - can start immediately

title: Foundation: Socket Connection Manager
description:
## What to build

Build the core SocketManager class that handles Unix Domain Socket connections to herdr. Expose `herdr_connect` and `herdr_disconnect` tools to the pi agent.

### SocketManager:
- Connect to Unix socket via `node:net`
- Socket path discovery (priority: HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env → HERDR_SESSION env → ~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock)
- Auto-connect on session_start, disconnect on session_shutdown
- Send JSON request with unique ID, match response by ID (handle out-of-order responses)
- Tracking pending requests (counter-based ID)
- Error handling: socket not found, connection refused, timeout

### Tools:
- `herdr_connect` — connect to herdr socket (optional params: session name, or custom socketPath). Returns connection status.
- `herdr_disconnect` — disconnect from herdr socket. Returns disconnected status.

### Files:
- `slices/socket/socket.types.ts` — SocketState enum, SocketConfig, PendingRequest
- `slices/socket/socket.manager.ts` — SocketManager class
- `slices/socket/socket.accessor.ts` — getSocketManager/setSocketManager singletons
- `slices/socket/socket.tool.ts` — herdr_connect + herdr_disconnect tool registration

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SocketManager connects to herdr Unix socket
- [ ] Socket path discovery respects env vars and falls back to default
- [ ] Can send JSON request and match response by ID
- [ ] Multiple concurrent requests handled correctly
- [ ] `herdr_connect` tool registered in pi
- [ ] `herdr_disconnect` tool registered in pi
- [ ] Auto-connect on session_start
- [ ] Clean disconnect on session_shutdown
- [ ] Clear error when socket not found

## Blocked by
None - can start immediately

title: Foundation: Socket Connection Manager
description:
## What to build

Build the core SocketManager class that handles Unix Domain Socket connections to herdr. Expose `herdr_connect` and `herdr_disconnect` tools to the pi agent.

### SocketManager:
- Connect to Unix socket via `node:net`
- Socket path discovery (priority: HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env → HERDR_SESSION env → ~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock)
- Auto-connect on session_start, disconnect on session_shutdown
- Send JSON request with unique ID, match response by ID (handle out-of-order responses)
- Tracking pending requests (counter-based ID)
- Error handling: socket not found, connection refused, timeout

### Tools:
- `herdr_connect` — connect to herdr socket (optional params: session name, or custom socketPath). Returns connection status.
- `herdr_disconnect` — disconnect from herdr socket. Returns disconnected status.

### Files:
- `slices/socket/socket.types.ts` — SocketState enum, SocketConfig, PendingRequest
- `slices/socket/socket.manager.ts` — SocketManager class
- `slices/socket/socket.accessor.ts` — getSocketManager/setSocketManager singletons
- `slices/socket/socket.tool.ts` — herdr_connect + herdr_disconnect tool registration

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SocketManager connects to herdr Unix socket
- [ ] Socket path discovery respects env vars and falls back to default
- [ ] Can send JSON request and match response by ID
- [ ] Multiple concurrent requests handled correctly
- [ ] `herdr_connect` tool registered in pi
- [ ] `herdr_disconnect` tool registered in pi
- [ ] Auto-connect on session_start
- [ ] Clean disconnect on session_shutdown
- [ ] Clear error when socket not found
